title: Johannesburg EMS warns motorists of dangerous road conditions as heavy rain hits Gauteng
text:
Johannesburg EMS warns motorists of dangerous road conditions as heavy rain hits Gauteng News Weather Johannesburg EMS warns motorists of dangerous road conditions as heavy rain hits Gauteng
 Wendy Dondolo | Published 6 hours ago Ask AI 1 min Johannesburg EMS has warned motorists to exercise caution on wet and slippery roads as heavy rain and thunderstorms affect parts of Gauteng. 
 Image: Wendy Dondolo 
 Johannesburg Emergency Management Services (EMS) has urged motorists to exercise extreme caution on wet and slippery roads as heavy rain and thunderstorms continue to affect parts of Gauteng on Tuesday.
 The emergency service warned drivers to maintain safe following distances and avoid crossing flooded roads and low-lying bridges as rainy conditions increase the risk of accidents.
 "It's raining in @CityofJoburgZA roads are wet and slippery motorists are urged to exercise caution while driving extend safe following distance avoid crossing flooded roads/low lying bridges, for any Life Threatening Emergencies call 011 375 5911," Johannesburg Emergency Services said.
 The warning comes as the South African Weather Service (SAWS) issued a Yellow Level 2 warning for severe thunderstorms, with localised flooding, hail and strong winds expected in parts of Gauteng.
 EMS urges motorists to avoid flooded roads
 Johannesburg EMS has cautioned motorists against driving through flooded areas, particularly low-lying bridges where rising water levels could pose a danger.
 Wet road surfaces can reduce traction and increase braking distances, making it more difficult for drivers to maintain control of their vehicles.
 Motorists are advised to reduce their speed, maintain a safe distance from other vehicles and remain alert to changing road conditions.
 Residents experiencing life-threatening emergencies have been urged to contact Johannesburg EMS
 SAWS warns of flooding and power disruptions
 Meanwhile, SAWS has warned that severe thunderstorms could bring heavy downpours, strong gusty winds and hail to parts of Gauteng.
 The Yellow Level 2 warning is valid from midday until 11:59pm on Tuesday.
 According to the weather service, the thunderstorms could cause localised flooding of low-water bridges and vulnerable settlements, as well as damage to property.
 Disruptions to electricity supply and communication networks are also possible.
 SAWS's rainfall forecast indicates a 60% probability of scattered showers and thunderstorms across parts of Gauteng.
 Residents and motorists have been urged to remain vigilant and monitor weather updates as the severe conditions persist.
